models.inverse_notes: Solve f_o=-M*f_e given M<0,f_e>0, or f_e=-f_o/M given f_o>0,M<0. Each has one positive root, retaining afocal spacing and original optical conditions. M=-20,f_e=0.03 -> f_o=0.6, then -0.6/0.03=-20. M=-1 gives identical focal lengths, not a singularity. M=0 has no finite positive-focal-length telescope in this profile; solving f_e would divide by zero, and solving f_o gives excluded zero focal length. An exactly on-axis object angle zero does not yield an independent measured ratio, although the paraxial linear angular response has this limit.
limitations: No statement about resolving power, brightness or lens aperture is implied by angular magnification alone.

Finite-object viewing, finite final-image distance, Galilean negative-eyepiece layout and separated principal-plane complications need an appropriate profile/revision; they are not silently assigned this derivation.

references.method: Value derived from published magnitude and sign: following Eq. 2.40, the source reports 40x for a 1 m objective and 2.5 cm eyepiece and explicitly says the minus sign denotes inversion. Under the signed output convention expected is -40, rather than falsely claiming the source prints -40. Tolerance 0.5 follows the displayed integer magnitude, not measured uncertainty.

Independent synthetic paraxial geometry: a field ray at +0.001 rad produces intermediate height +0.0006 m in the objective focal plane. The corresponding exit angle from the shared eyepiece focal plane is -0.0006/0.03=-0.020 rad, giving angle ratio -20. Uses two focal-plane triangles, not replay of the serialized focal ratio. Tolerance is decimal floating-point allowance.

Symmetry limit: two identical positive lenses separated by twice their focal length relay small incoming angles with equal magnitude and opposite orientation. An afocal unit-angle inverter is a legitimate boundary, not zero power for an individual lens.

models.inverse_notes: Solve f=(L-ell)/(M*L/N-1) given N>0,L>=N,0<=ell<L: require M*L/N-1>0 for f>0, then original guards. Solve L=N*(f-ell)/(M*f-N): require denominator!=0, N>0,f>0,ell>=0, and reconstructed L>=N,L>ell. Check M=3.48,N=0.3,L=0.5,ell=0.02 gives f=0.1; invert L from those values to recover 0.5, then forward gives 3.48. If ell=f, forward M=N/f independent of every admissible finite L; L is underdetermined when that equality holds, inconsistent otherwise. If ell!=f but M=N/f, only the L->infinity limit exists, outside finite L. At ell=0,L=N, M=1+N/f; as L->infinity with fixed ell, M->N/f. No separate special-case models. Solving N or ell not separately numerically tested.
limitations: Finite L does not serialize the relaxed-eye infinite-image case; its limit M=N/f is documented rather than duplicated as another record.
The source's familiar N/f to 1+N/f range assumes the lens close to the eye; it is not imposed at arbitrary ell, especially ell>f.
Does not predict a person's acuity, comfort, retinal image quality or aberration; near point and focusing ability must be independently supplied.

references.method: Published Example 2.10(a) requires M=15 mm/3.0 mm=5.0 and reports f=6.3 cm. Tolerance 0.05 is half the final 0.1 magnification reporting step and covers this 0.0317 difference; no exact 6.25 cm is silently substituted.

Independent synthetic two-ray construction: 0.001 m object at distance 12/145 m (0.0827586206896552) from a 0.1 m lens. Center ray y=-(145/12)*0.001*x and parallel/focal ray y=0.001-0.010*x intersect at x=-0.48 m,y=0.0058 m. Eye 0.02 m behind lens sees it at 0.50 m: angle=0.0058/0.5=0.0116. Unaided same-height angle at N=0.3 is 0.001/0.3; their ratio is 3.48. This computes ray/angle geometry rather than the serialized expression. Exact synthetic lengths, decimal rounding tolerance.

assumptions: Source definition: object speed and sound speed refer to the same medium reference frame and ambient state.
Source condition: sound speed depends on gas/material and state; no universal air-speed value is a reusable default.

gaps: Add mach_number and wave_phase_speed; generic speed already exists and is reused only with an explicit medium-relative magnitude definition/context. Units 1 and m/s supported. Do not equate Mach number with a perceived frequency ratio.

models.inverse_notes: Inverse u=M_a*v requires M_a>=0,v>0; unique, including u=0 for M_a=0. Inverse v=u/M_a requires M_a>0,u>0; unique positive v. Example M_a=1.5,v=300 -> u=450, forward restores 1.5. M_a=0,u=0 leaves v undetermined across all positive values; M_a=0,u>0 is inconsistent, not an infinite-speed solution within finite inputs. At M_a=1, u=v and either inverse is regular; no subsonic Doppler guard should be imported into this independent definition.
limitations: Does not determine shock geometry, drag, heating, intensity or pressure; those require additional source-supported relationships.
A local flow Mach number and free-stream flight Mach number cannot be bound without matching the speed and sound-speed locations/frames.
No ordinary sound-speed definition exists in vacuum; do not manufacture a zero denominator or vacuum acoustic medium.

references.method: Independent synthetic common-time comparison: in two seconds the object travels 900 m and a small sound disturbance travels 600 m, so the object advances one and a half sound-propagation distances. This equal-time distance ratio is the same defining nondimensional comparison without replaying u/v. Exact synthetic distances, floating-point allowance.

Definition boundary: equal object and sound speeds are Mach one, as explicitly identified in NASA's regime discussion. Sound speed 340 is an arbitrary supplied example value, not a standard-air default.

Zero-motion identity: an object at rest relative to its acoustic medium travels none of the sound-propagation distance, so its Mach number is zero. 1480 m/s is a synthetic supplied medium value without claimed water-state calibration.

rejection_cases.reason: A positive acoustic speed is required; zero makes the ratio undefined and is not a vacuum sound-speed model.
Matching ambient sound speed must be supplied; speed alone does not determine Mach number.

relationship.locator: University Physics 1 Eq. 17.21; NASA Glenn Mach Number opening ratio definition
relationship.translation_notes: Local M_a maps to source M and u to the source's nonnegative speed magnitude v_s relative to the acoustic medium. v is sound speed in that same medium state, not a generic spacecraft vacuum speed. Both units m/s have scale 1 and their ratio is dimensionless: (L*T^-1)/(L*T^-1)=1. Sonic M_a=1 is admissible for this definition even though a separate ordinary Doppler frequency formula is singular there. No speed-of-sound material law or assumed numerical sound speed is included.

sources.evidence: Mach number is the source speed relative to the medium divided by sound speed. Sonic and supersonic source motion is discussed separately from the subsonic Doppler expression.

assumptions: Source geometry: one emitted pulse travels to the reflector and back to the co-located receiver.

Application profile for this derivation: transducer and reflector stationary relative to one homogeneous resting medium, equal straight outbound/return paths, constant pulse speed and negligible or corrected reflection/electronics delay.

Source qualification: real hydrographic sound-speed variation can bend paths, so this single-speed straight-path profile must be checked before use. The air echo illustration supports acoustic use beyond water.

constants.locator: Active Sonar, emission and reflected echo return to the same transducer; equal-leg assumption is the explicitly declared application profile
constants.meaning: Two equal geometric path legs (outbound plus return) for a co-located stationary transmitter/receiver and reflector; not a unit conversion.

gaps: Add pulse_propagation_speed, round_trip_acoustic_time and acoustic_target_range. m/s,s,m units supported. Keep pulse speed distinct from wave_phase_speed without a nondispersive compatibility argument. This measurement protocol is not a renamed uniform-motion catalog model.

models.inverse_notes: Inverse tau=2*r/v_p requires r>0,v_p>0 and the original stationary reciprocal-path assumptions; unique. Inverse v_p=2*r/tau requires r>0,tau>0; unique, but an inferred path speed is not automatically a local material phase speed. Example r=300,v_p=1500 gives tau=0.4 s; forward substitution restores 300 m. At r=0 and tau=0 there is a mathematical zero-path limit but no separated-reflector echo in this profile, and the speed inverse is underdetermined. Zero tau with positive range is inconsistent for finite pulse speed. No moving-target or finite-processing-delay inverse is claimed.
limitations: Moving/bistatic endpoints, currents, curved refracted paths or variable sound-speed profiles require more kinematics/ray tracing.
The measured range is not automatically seafloor vertical depth; beam geometry, transducer draft, attitude and tide/datum corrections are separate.
Not a pulse-energy, echo-amplitude or detectability model; timing an identifiable return is assumed.

references.method: Independent constructed flight itinerary for a reflector 300 m away: with supplied constant pulse speed 1500 m/s, each 300 m leg takes 0.2 s, and emission-to-return elapsed time is 0.4 s. Expected is the constructed one-way geometric range 300 m, not a replay of v_p*tau/2. Synthetic homogeneous-medium data; no universal seawater speed assumed. Tolerance covers decimal arithmetic.

references.method: Independent constructed reflector at 5.1 m with outbound and return event times 0.015 s each at supplied 340 m/s. relationship.original_equation: Prose: emit an acoustic pulse, receive its reflected echo, use emission-to-reception elapsed time to measure range. Derived equal-path specialization: 2*r=v_p*tau.
relationship.translation_notes: Introduce r as one-way range, tau as round-trip elapsed acoustic propagation time and v_p as the appropriate constant pulse-pattern speed. NOAA prose supplies out-and-back measurement geometry, and the source's constant-speed pulse law gives total traveled length=v_p*tau. For co-located stationary endpoints and same straight reciprocal path, total length=r+r, hence divisor 2, attributed as the two-leg geometry, not a unit conversion. (L*T^-1)*T/1=L. This is an explicitly derived measurement relation, not a claim that NOAA prints this exact symbolic equation. Do not replace pulse speed with a dispersive medium's phase speed. It is distinguished from uniform one-way translation by the independently meaningful round-trip measurement protocol.

sources.evidence: An active transducer emits an acoustic pulse, receives its reflected echo, and uses elapsed round-trip time to infer target range. The displayed prose does not itself supply a universal speed or a full moving-platform/ray-tracing formula.

models.summary: Source-backed equal-path kinematic derivation for a separated stationary reflector and co-located stationary acoustic transmitter/receiver, using a supplied constant pulse speed. The output is one-way range, not total traveled path or datum-corrected depth.
models.title: One-way acoustic range from stationary round-trip echo time

variables.context: Same co-located stationary acoustic transmitter/receiver and separated stationary reflector, same medium rest frame and acoustic pulse mode. The ray follows the same straight path out and back through a homogeneous resting medium at a constant supplied pulse speed; tau is emission-to-echo reception elapsed time after any fixed electronics/reflection delay correction.
variables.definition: Positive speed of the identifiable acoustic pulse feature used for timing along both path legs.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive constant, supplied for pulse band and medium state; matches phase speed only with separate nondispersive support.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced v_p maps to sound/pulse propagation speed in the source prose

variables.context: Same co-located stationary acoustic transmitter/receiver and separated stationary reflector, same medium rest frame and acoustic pulse mode. The ray follows the same straight path out and back through a homogeneous resting medium at a constant supplied pulse speed; tau is emission-to-echo reception elapsed time after any fixed electronics/reflection delay correction.
variables.definition: Continuous elapsed two-way acoustic propagation time from emission to reception of the same reflected pulse, corrected for any fixed nonpropagation delay.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive for the separated reflector; not one-way time, repetition period, pulse duration or accumulated active hours.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced tau maps to emission-to-echo reception time

variables.context: Same co-located stationary acoustic transmitter/receiver and separated stationary reflector, same medium rest frame and acoustic pulse mode. The ray follows the same straight path out and back through a homogeneous resting medium at a constant supplied pulse speed; tau is emission-to-echo reception elapsed time after any fixed electronics/reflection delay correction.
variables.definition: Positive one-way straight acoustic path distance from transducer to the specified reflecting target under the stationary reciprocal-path profile.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive for a separated reflector; not automatically vertical water depth or elevation relative to a datum.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced r maps to target range inferred from echo timing
